subject.title: Telegram owner commands: trusted execution mode for approval-gated actions

question: Should OpenClaw add a trusted-owner approval-bypass mode for Telegram group-origin privileged actions, and should that live as a shared execution policy instead of a Telegram-only config boolean?
rationale: The source evidence proves the requested mode is missing, but adding it intentionally changes when channel identity may skip privileged-action approval prompts, which is a security boundary and config-contract decision automation should not choose.

options.title: Design shared trusted-owner policy
options.body: Add a disabled-by-default policy with explicit sender, allowlisted group, action-class, destructive-operation, audit, docs, and regression-test semantics across the existing approval stack.

options.title: Keep current approval model
options.body: Decline the bypass and document that operators who want no prompts should deliberately use existing elevated full plus permissive host approval policy.

options.title: Add Telegram-only shortcut
options.body: Implement the proposed Telegram setting directly, accepting a smaller patch but higher risk of policy drift from shared approvals and elevated execution.

recommendation.title: Design shared trusted-owner policy
recommendation.body: Add a disabled-by-default policy with explicit sender, allowlisted group, action-class, destructive-operation, audit, docs, and regression-test semantics across the existing approval stack.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans elevated execution, approval policy, security posture, and config-surface direction, and the strongest history signal routes those areas through steipete.
